LESSON: SIGN READING 9.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Sign Reading 9.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 9.2.1 Fluency, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly? 2. How does correct pronunciation help us in reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 9.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Citizenship: Information and communication skills are enhanced; learners learn about friendship as a basis for social cohesion and demonstrate interest

in interacting with others.

Values:
• Respect: acceptance enhanced as the learner understands and appreciates the importance of friendship.

• Unity: cooperation is enhanced as the learner takes turn in performing activities and in conversation

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: social cohesion is nurtured as the learners learn about social relationships.

Suggested Learning Resources:

By the end of the sub strand, the

learner should be able to:

a) recognise signs of common

and proper nouns from texts,

b) identify people, things or places

around them by name from texts,

c) use signs of common and

proper nouns in short

sentences,

d) appreciate the importance of

identifying objects, places or

things by name.

● In groups, learners are guided to

observe, fingerspell and sign

vocabulary related to proper

nouns.

● Individually, the learner is guided to

name the places, people or things

around them collaboratively, for

example,

- places – Nairobi,

- people – teacher, mother, brother

- things – chair, desk, pen

● Individually, the learner is guided

to single out and sign common and

proper nouns from a text.

● In groups, learners name items in the

classroom.

● In pairs, learners are guided to talk

about their friends as they sign using

common and proper nouns in pairs.

● Individually, the learner is guided to

talk about what their friends like as

they sign using common and proper

nouns.

● Individually, the learner is guided to

fill in blank spaces using

common and proper nouns.

you see in the

classroom?

to refer to people

and places by their

names?
